stem.text: A lamp is suspended in equilibrium from a fixed support by three long identical wires.

stem.alt: Lamp hanging from a fixed support by three wires; labels: wires, fixed support, lamp.

stem.text: The weight of the lamp causes each wire to have an extension of $0.40\,\text{cm}$. The height $h$ of the lamp above the floor is measured.
The middle wire suddenly breaks and the lamp falls a small distance as the extensions of the remaining two wires increase. The wires obey Hooke’s law.
When the lamp is in equilibrium, the height $h$ of the lamp above the floor is measured again.
What is the difference between the two values of $h$?
